diagnostics.message: aws_eks_cluster.cluster only references aws_iam_role.cluster.arn, but the required cluster policies are attached by aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.cluster, which has no ordering edge to the cluster. The AWS provider documents that the EKS cluster must depend on the IAM role policy attachments, otherwise EKS cannot create/delete managed EC2 infrastructure (e.g. security groups) because the role lacks AmazonEKSClusterPolicy at the time. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.cluster]` to the cluster.

aws_eks_cluster.cluster sets enabled_cluster_log_types from var.eks_enabled_log_types, and aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster manages the exact control-plane log group name (/aws/eks/${var.name_prefix}/cluster) that EKS auto-creates when log types are enabled. There is no ordering edge between them, so the cluster can be created first, letting EKS create the log group and causing the Terraform aws_cloudwatch_log_group creation to fail with AlreadyExists. Add `depends_on = [aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster]` to the cluster.

module.eks_node_group_al2023 references aws_iam_role.eks_node_group.arn (create_iam_role = false), but that role's worker-node policies are attached by aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.eks_node_group, which has no ordering edge to the node group. The managed node group's instances will fail to join the cluster (missing AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy etc.) if the node group is created before the attachments. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.eks_node_group]` to the node group module.
